title: US forces enter Iran by..?
description:

The resolution source will be a consensus of credible reporting.

eventMetadata.context_description: US special forces conducted a rescue operation inside Iranian territory on April 1-3, extracting a downed pilot after two US aircraft were shot down amid escalating airstrikes in the ongoing US-Israel-Iran conflict, now in its sixth week since February 28 launch targeting Iranian nuclear sites, missile facilities, and command centers. Massive US deployments—including Marine Expeditionary Units, the 82nd Airborne, and over 50,000 troops in the region—signal preparations for potential ground operations to secure key assets like nuclear materials, though no large-scale invasion has occurred. President Trump vows continued hard strikes, while Iran retaliates with missiles at Israel and Gulf targets, warning of severe resistance to any boots-on-the-ground incursion; traders weigh these signals against historical reluctance for prolonged Middle East ground wars.

eventMetadata.context_description: Spain edges France and England as the slim trader favorite at 16% implied probability to claim the 2026 FIFA World Cup, propelled by their Euro 2024 success, flawless qualifiers, and emerging talents like Lamine Yamal and Pedri maintaining peak form. France climbed after March friendlies crushing Brazil and Colombia to top FIFA rankings, boosting Mbappé-led attack, while England dipped post-shock Japan defeat despite Bellingham's influence. Argentina clings to contention via Messi's legacy and Copa momentum, but Brazil fades amid Rodrygo and Alisson injuries. Tight top-five odds under 16% underscore 48-team depth, balanced group draws, host advantages for USA-Mexico-Canada, and pre-tournament volatility from late scratches or tune-ups.

title: US x Iran ceasefire by...?
description:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if there is an official ceasefire agreement, defined as a publicly announced and mutually agreed halt in direct military engagement, between the United States and Iran by the listed date, 11:59 PM ET.

For the purposes of this market, an “official ceasefire agreement” requires clear public confirmation from both the United States government and the government of Iran that they have agreed to halt military hostilities against one another, or for an official ceasefire agreement to be otherwise confirmed to have been reached by an overwhelming consensus of media reporting.

If the agreement is officially reached before the resolution date, this market will resolve to “Yes,” regardless of whether the ceasefire officially takes effect after the resolution date.

Any form of informal understanding, backchannel communication, de-escalation without an announced agreement, or unilateral pause in hostilities will not be considered an official ceasefire. Humanitarian pauses, limited operational pauses, or temporary tactical stand-downs will not count toward the resolution of this market.

A broader peace deal, normalization agreement, or political framework will qualify only if it includes a publicly announced and mutually agreed halt in military engagement between the United States and Iran, effective on a specified date, or otherwise confirmed by an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting. Agreements that outline future negotiations or de-escalation measures without an explicit, dated commitment to stop fighting will not qualify.

This market’s resolution will be based on official statements from the United States government and the government of Iran. However, an overwhelming consensus of credible media reporting confirming that an official ceasefire agreement has been reached will suffice.

eventMetadata.context_description: The Indiana Pacers enter their matchup against the Charlotte Hornets severely depleted by injuries, with star point guard Tyrese Haliburton sidelined by a season-ending right Achilles tear, Andrew Nembhard out (back soreness), T.J. McConnell out (hamstring), and others like Johnny Furphy (ACL) unavailable, forcing a makeshift lineup anchored by available forward Pascal Siakam (cleared right knee management). Charlotte, holding an 40-36 record and 8th in the East amid play-in contention, boasts a healthier roster including LaMelo Ball (available), Brandon Miller, and Miles Bridges at home, despite Moussa Diabate (ankle) and Grant Williams (management) out. Pacers languish at 18-58, eliminated from playoffs, after Hornets' dominant 133-109 win in February; recent Pacers form underscores defensive woes and backcourt voids driving trader consensus toward Charlotte's advantages in momentum, home court, and matchup edges.
